{{short description|In physics: electromagnetic momentum within dielectric media}}

The '''Abraham–Minkowski controversy''' is a [[physics]] debate concerning [[Momentum#In electromagnetics|electromagnetic momentum]] within [[dielectric]] media.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Leonhardt|first=Ulf|year=2006|title=Momentum in an uncertain light|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=444|issue=7121|pages=823–824|bibcode=2006Natur.444..823L|doi=10.1038/444823a|pmid=17167461|s2cid=33682507|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=McDonald1>{{Cite web|last=McDonald|first=K. T.|year=2017|title=Bibliography on the Abraham–Minkowski Debate|url=http://physics.princeton.edu/~mcdonald/examples/ambib.pdf|access-date=2018-05-23|archive-date=2022-01-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120050111/https://physics.princeton.edu//~mcdonald/examples/ambib.pdf}}</ref> Two equations were first suggested by [[Hermann Minkowski]] (1908)<ref name=Minkowski1>{{cite journal|last=Minkowski|first=H.|year=1908|title=Die Grundgleichungen für die elektromagnetischen Vorgänge in bewegten Körpern|journal=Nachrichten von der Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-Physikalische Klasse|pages=53–111|title-link=s:de:Die Grundgleichungen für die elektromagnetischen Vorgänge in bewegten Körpern}}
:* Wikisource translation: [https://en.wikisource.org/?curid=674267 The Fundamental Equations for Electromagnetic Processes in Moving Bodies]
</ref> and [[Max Abraham]] (1909)<ref name=Abraham1>{{cite journal|last=Abraham|first=M.|year=1909|title=Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper|journal=[[Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo]]|volume=28|pages=1–28|doi=10.1007/bf03018208|title-link=s:de:Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper (Abraham)|s2cid=121681939}}
:* Wikisource translation: [[s:On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies (Abraham)|On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies]]
</ref><ref name="Abraham2">{{cite journal |last=Abraham |first=M. |year=1910 |title=Sull'Elettrodinamica di Minkowski |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1428452 |journal=[[Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo]] |volume=30 |pages=33–46 |doi=10.1007/bf03014862 |s2cid=121524871}}
:* Wikisource translation: [[wikisource:On the Electrodynamics of Minkowski|On the Electrodynamics of Minkowski]]
</ref> for this momentum. They predict different values, from which the name of the controversy derives.<ref name=Pfeifer1>{{cite journal|last2=Nieminen|first2=T. A|last3=Heckenberg|first3=N. R.|last4=Rubinsztein-Dunlop|first4=H.|year=2007|title=''Colloquium:'' Momentum of an electromagnetic wave in dielectric media|journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]|volume=79|issue=4|pages=1197–1216|arxiv=0710.0461|bibcode=2007RvMP...79.1197P|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.79.1197|last1=Pfeifer|first1=R. N. C.}} See also: {{cite journal|year=2009|title=Erratum: ''Colloquium:'' Momentum of an electromagnetic wave in dielectric media [Rev. Mod. Phys. '''79''', 1197 (2007)]|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=81|issue=1|page=443|bibcode=2009RvMP...81..443P|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.81.443|arxiv=0710.0461|last1=Pfeifer|first1=Robert N. C.|last2=Nieminen|first2=Timo A.|last3=Heckenberg|first3=Norman R.|last4=Rubinsztein-Dunlop|first4=Halina}}</ref> Experimental support has been claimed for both.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=A. Ashkin |author2=J. M. Dziedzic |title=Radiation Pressure on a Free Liquid Surface |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=1973 |volume=30 |issue=4 |pages=139–142 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.139 |bibcode=1973PhRvL..30..139A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Gretchen K. Campbell |author2=Aaron E. Leanhardt |author3=Jongchul Mun |author4=Micah Boyd |author5=Erik W. Streed |author6=Wolfgang Ketterle |author7=David E. Pritchard |title=Photon Recoil Momentum in Dispersive Media |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2005 |volume=94 |issue=17 |article-number=170403 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170403|pmid=15904272 |arxiv=cond-mat/0502014 |bibcode=2005PhRvL..94q0403C |s2cid=2033128 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Weilong She |author2=Jianhui Yu |author3=Raohui Feng |title=Observation of a Push Force on the End Face of a Nanometer Silica Filament Exerted by Outgoing Light |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2008 |volume=101 |issue=24 |article-number=243601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.243601|pmid=19113619 |arxiv=0806.2442 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.101x3601S |s2cid=9630919 }}</ref><ref name=Dacey1>{{cite web|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/experiment-resolves-century-old-optics-mystery/|title=Experiment resolves century-old optics mystery|last=Dacey|first=J.|date=9 January 2009|work=[[Physics World]]|access-date=18 April 2021}}</ref> Physicist [[Vitaly Ginzburg]] called it a perpetual problem.<ref name="McDonald1" /> 

The two points of view have different physical interpretations and thus neither need be more correct than the other.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Milonni |first1=Peter W. |last2=Boyd |first2=Robert W. |date=2010-12-31 |title=Momentum of Light in a Dielectric Medium |url=http://www.hajim.rochester.edu/optics/sites/boyd/assets/pdf/publications/Milonni_AOP_10.pdf |journal=Advances in Optics and Photonics |language=en |volume=2 |issue=4 |page=519 |doi=10.1364/AOP.2.000519 |bibcode=2010AdOP....2..519M |issn=1943-8206 |access-date=2023-07-19}}</ref>
[[David J. Griffiths]] argues that, in the presence of matter, only the total [[stress–energy tensor]] carries unambiguous physical significance; how one apportions it between an "electromagnetic" part and a "matter" part depends on context and convenience.<ref name=Griffiths1>{{Cite journal|last=Griffiths|first=D. J.|year=2012|title=Resource Letter EM-1: Electromagnetic Momentum|journal=American Journal of Physics|volume=80|issue=1|pages=7–18|doi=10.1119/1.3641979|bibcode = 2012AmJPh..80....7G|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The controversy is still claimed to have importance in [[physics beyond the Standard Model]] where electrodynamics gets modifications, like in the presence of [[Axion|axions]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tobar |first1=Michael E. |last2=McAllister |first2=Ben T. |last3=Goryachev |first3=Maxim |date=2022-02-15 |title=Poynting vector controversy in axion modified electrodynamics |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.105.045009 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=105 |issue=4 |article-number=045009 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.105.045009 |issn=2470-0010|arxiv=2109.04056 |bibcode=2022PhRvD.105d5009T |s2cid=246430570 }}</ref>

== Equations ==
In SI units, the equations describe electromagnetic momentum and are given by<ref name="McDonald1" />
{| class="wikitable"
|+
!Minkoskwi
!Abraham
|-
|<math>\textbf{P} = \textbf{D} \times \textbf{B}</math>
|<math>\textbf{P} = \frac{\textbf{E} \times \textbf{H}}{c^2}</math>
|}
:

where:
*<math>\textbf{P}</math> is the density of electromagnetic momentum
*<math>\textbf{D}</math> is the [[electric displacement field]]
*<math>\textbf{B}</math> is the [[magnetic flux density]]

*<math>\textbf{E}</math> is the [[electric field]]
*<math>\textbf{H}</math> is the [[magnetizing field]]
*<math>c^2</math> is the [[speed of light]] squared

=== Consequences ===
According to Abraham, the momentum of an [[Electromagnetic radiation|electromagnetic wave]] in a medium should be slower. Minkowski predicts that the momentum should be larger.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cho |first=Adrian |date=2004 |title=Momentum From Nothing |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevFocus.13.3 |journal=Focus |language=en |volume=13 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevFocus.13.3 |issn=1539-0748}}</ref>

For a finite-lenght [[optical fiber]] emitting light at one of its ends, it is unclear if the fiber recoils backs in the direction of the light emission (as predicted by Abraham) or if the fiber is pulled in the direction of emission (as predicted by Minkowski).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schirber |first=Michael |date=2008 |title=Light Bends Glass |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevFocus.22.20 |journal=Focus |language=en |volume=22 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevFocus.22.20 |issn=1539-0748}}</ref>
